english.title: Offer / promise / give financial / other advantage knowing acceptance was improper performance of function / activity
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[offered]_
(B)_[promised]_
(C)_[gave]_

a financial or other advantage to another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), knowing or believing that acceptance of the advantage would constitute the improper performance of a relevant function or activity, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FUNCTION OR ACTIVITY..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(3) and 11 of the Bribery Act 2010.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For bribery offences under section 1 of the Bribery Act 2010 see H100582, and for conspiracy to bribe H100583.
(ii) Section 1(4) of the Act provides that it does not matter whether the person to whom the advantage is offered, promised or given is the same person as the person who is to perform, or has performed, the function or activity concerned.
(iii) Section 1(5) provides that it does not matter whether the advantage is offered, promised or given directly or through a third party.
(iv) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office, section 10.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.Notes:
The reference to 12 months is to be read as 6 months in relation to an offence committed before the commencement of paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Where any person other than an individual, e.g. a company, is convicted of this offence:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
